claims.text: The starting alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The starting HfNbTaTiZr is in the cast state.
Cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxidation resistance for high-temperature use in air.
Pre-oxidation at about 950 °C and an oxygen partial pressure of 10^-4–10^-3 bar for 2–3 hours will generate a protective oxide scale.
Low-pressure nitriding at about 950 °C and a nitrogen partial pressure of 10^-4–10^-3 bar for 2–3 hours will generate a protective nitride scale.
Air or rapid cooling after treatment will lock in the protective scale.
The treatment will produce a thin, dense, adherent layer without significantly changing the bulk alloy composition.
The oxide or nitride scale will act as a diffusion barrier and slow oxygen ingress.
Oxygen ingress causes embrittlement along grain boundaries in HfNbTaTiZr.
High-temperature deformation and mechanical properties are controlled primarily by dislocations and their morphology and density.
Reducing oxygen ingress will preserve the dislocation-mediated deformation mechanisms responsible for useful mechanical performance.
The surface treatment will improve oxidation resistance in oxygen-containing atmospheres at temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The treatment will cause minimal or no reduction in room-temperature tensile ductility relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The treatment will cause minimal or no reduction in high-temperature yield strength at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Excessive scale thickening or spallation could impair ductility or load-bearing capability.

contradictions.description: The proposal does not specify a single intervention: it alternates between pre-oxidation and nitriding, oxide and nitride scales, and low-O2 and low-N2 environments. These are distinct treatments and mechanisms rather than one defined intervention.
